title: Greeting Generator
story: You're building a chatbot that greets visitors to your website. "Good morning" at 9 AM feels warm, "Good evening" at 8 PM feels right — the same "hello" all day feels lazy. Your bot needs to know the time of day!
why: Conditional logic inside functions powers personalized experiences. Based on input, the function chooses different behavior — the foundation of smart programs.
analogy: A greeting function is like a friendly doorman who checks their watch and adjusts their welcome — "Good morning!" at sunrise, "Good evening!" at sunset.
try_it: Add a `get_time_emoji` function that returns a sun emoji "(sun)" for morning, "(coffee)" for afternoon, and "(moon)" for evening. Then combine it with your greet function!
tips: Use `&&` to combine two conditions: `hour >= 5 && hour < 12` means 'at least 5 AND less than 12'
Ranges should NOT overlap: 5-11, 12-16, 17-20, then else catches 21-4
The `else` is your safety net — it handles all times that don't fit your categories
common_mistakes: Overlapping ranges: `hour >= 5 && hour < 13` and `hour >= 12 && hour < 17` both match 12
Using `||` (OR) instead of `&&` (AND) — `hour >= 5 || hour < 12` is true for ALL hours
Forgetting the `else` — what happens at 3 AM? Without `else`, the function might not return anything
